memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and they waved them before the LORD as a wave offering. Then Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering as an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the LORD." - Lev 8:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Watch the movement here. Moses puts the offering into their hands. They wave it before God. Then Moses takes it back from their hands and burns it.

Given, held, offered, surrendered.

The Hebrew word for the ordination offering literally means "filling of the hands." Aaron's hands were filled — and then emptied onto the altar.

That is the shape of every calling. God fills your hands with something: a gift, an opportunity, a family, a ministry, a season of usefulness. And it is genuinely yours to hold. But it was always meant to be offered back.

David understood this at the end of his life, having gathered enormous resources for the temple: Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from your hand (1 Chr 29:14).

The danger for anyone who serves is to be filled and never emptied — to accumulate influence, reputation, or resources and quietly begin to hold them as possessions rather than offerings.

Filled hands are a gift. Emptied hands are worship.

What has God put in your hands lately? And have you waved it before Him yet?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God filled my hands with in this season?
2. Am I holding it as a possession or offering it back to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You fill my hands with good things. Teach me to lift them back to You rather than closing my fingers around them. Amen.
